question: In a video made public on 11 July 20251, a whistleblower accuses Laura Kövesi, the European Chief Prosecutor, of covering up an order issued by M.B. – the head of the Operations and College Support Unit at the European Public Prosecutor’s Office – to destroy evidence. ‘He decides if something can disappear or not’.

The files that were deliberately destroyed allegedly implicated corrupt politicians in Romania accused of misusing EU funds. C.B., a former legal adviser at the EPPO, states in the video2 that he was ordered to destroy 71 files, including ‘ESRR_2021_19_01’, and that he informed the Chief Prosecutor before doing so.

We contacted the Dutch coordinator of the SOLARIS project3 – funded by the Commission to the tune of EUR 2.7 million – seeking his expertise in detecting and mitigating fake videos published on social media for reasons of political disinformation. He stated, however, that he did not have such expertise and offered no further support. 1.
Are the Commission and the European Anti-Fraud Office (OLAF) aware of this video alleging the destruction of evidence at the EPPO, and have they checked whether the video is real or fake?
Which independent authority is responsible for investigating the allegations that evidence has been destroyed at the EPPO? Is it OLAF? Is it the European Data Protection Supervisor?
Has OLAF opened an investigation into these allegations of serious misconduct by EU officials4?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (27.1.2026) The Commission does not have any information additional to what is publicly available regarding this case.

The European Anti-Fraud Office (OLAF) is responsible for conducting administrative investigations concerning fraud, corruption and any other illegal activity affecting the financial interests of the EU, as well as suspicions of serious misconduct by EU staff and members of the EU institutions. OLAF does not have the authority to conduct criminal investigations.

OLAF is independent from the Commission in the exercise of its investigative function. OLAF does not usually issue comments on cases that it may or may not be treating. This is in order to protect the confidentiality of any possible investigations and possible subsequent follow-up procedures, as well as to ensure respect for personal data and procedural rights.

Finally, the Commission recalls that the European Data Protection Supervisor, whose mandate is set out in Regulation (EU) 2018/17251, is tasked with monitoring and ensuring that EU institutions and bodies process personal data in compliance with the applicable data protection framework.
